# Quantum Coherent Collisions

This repository studies exact heralded coordinatewise amplitude powers of an
unknown pure state from supplied copies, their optimal worst-case copy cost,
unknown-moment calibration, and an explicitly charged collective implementation.
The scientific account is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, principal copy law, baseline comparison,
  direct proof route, selected educational anchor, reproduction command,
  and purpose and contact.
- science/README.md: connected account and proof dependencies.
- science/model.md: authoritative input model, coherent target, charged resources,
  success and fidelity conventions, expected versus hard budgets, fixed-power
  scope, and exact profile-minimax consequence.
- science/coherent_extraction.md: symmetric occupation expansion, successful
  Kraus instrument, validity, exact output-residual factorization, success
  identity, constant-success batch, and hard-budget geometric schedule.
- science/unknown_moment.md: first-r-collision pilot, Poissonized mean bound,
  exact rational batch selection, independent fresh coherent block, renewal
  accounting, stopping bound, and realized-memory distinction.
- science/converse.md: arbitrary successful CP maps, torus twirling, charge
  blocks, hard-budget theorem, success-weighted fidelity, explicit failure
  of an unweighted conditional average, expected-budget bound, and exact
  fixed-profile phase-minimax theorem.
- science/implementation.md: Boolean eligibility projection, charged inverse
  repeated-list symmetrization, bounded-run permutation resources, sparse
  reversible extraction, multiplicity rotation, record cleanup, gates,
  storage, connectivity, and finite-synthesis conditional error.
- science/interpretation.md: coherent output versus classical collision samples,
  phase multiplication, effective support, structured promises, and resource limits.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: primary attribution and precise model comparisons,
  including the supplied-copy Fourier-support predecessor, source-unitary
  transforms, qubit filters, covariance, collisions and symmetrization.
- references/references.bib: bibliographic metadata.
- verification/README.md: reproducibility commands, finite coverage and limits.
- verification/check_science.py: deterministic standard-library verification runner.

Learning entrypoints:
- learning/MILESTONES.md: the canonical project map, exactly M01-M30;
  11 background/preliminaries milestones and 19 narrative/innovation milestones,
  with questions, understanding targets, earlier dependencies, conceptual
  connections and scientific references.
- learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md: the single selected educational anchor,
  John Watrous's The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), with verified
  section routes, notation and convention translation, and project connections.
- Author's book page: https://jhwatrous.github.io/books-and-courses.html
- Author's complete manuscript: https://jhwatrous.github.io/TQI.pdf

Reader routes:
- To understand the story: begin with science/model.md; follow exact extraction,
  unknown-moment adaptation and the converse; read implementation for the charged
  operations and connect the conclusions in science/interpretation.md.
- For self-directed study: use the Watrous bridge alongside M01-M30. The common
  map follows the project's dependencies rather than a particular reader's
  starting knowledge. Primary research papers supply attribution and imported
  ingredients; they are not additional assigned textbooks.
- To inspect a theorem: first read science/model.md for its quantifiers and
  metrics, then the full relevant proof file and primary source attribution.
  An introductory explanation or milestone target is not a substitute for
  the theorem's hypotheses or proof.
- To reproduce a finite ingredient: read verification/README.md, then run
  python3 verification/check_science.py from the repository root.
  Python 3.10 or later and the standard library suffice. Distinguish a fresh
  execution from a documented reference result.

Preserve these distinctions when explaining or editing:
- The supplied resource is identical copies of one unknown pure state.
  Preparation unitaries, adjoints, source reflections, amplitude oracles,
  QRAM and phase-dependent side information are different access models.
- The output is a normalized coherent state with amplitudes alpha_i^r.
  Sampling only its computational-basis distribution does not solve the task.
- The known basis matters. A global phase does not change the output density
  operator, but relative phases are multiplied by r.
- r is a fixed integer at least two. O_r and Theta_r hide r-dependent constants;
  no favorable growing-r complexity is claimed.
- All copies are charged, including calibration, rejected coherent batches and
  retries. The moment-adaptive O_r(S_r^(-1/r)) guarantee is an expectation,
  not a deterministic instance-sized copy or workspace cap.
- The geometric schedule gives a separate O_r(N^(1-1/r)) hard budget with
  constant success. The robust matching lower bound also extends to expected
  costs under its stated success-weighted accuracy condition.
- Exact profile-minimax optimality fixes a nontrivial amplitude profile and
  permits all continuous phases, even when the profile is known. It is not
  constant-error instance optimality for every profile or promised family.
- For heralded maps, twirl the unnormalized successful map. Average target
  overlap equals average success times success-weighted conditional fidelity.
  An unweighted average of conditional fidelity is insufficient; see the
  explicit one-copy counterexample in science/converse.md.
- The project's pure-target fidelity is target population, the square of the
  root-fidelity convention used by Watrous. Trace distance includes the
  one-half factor. Consult the bridge before translating inequalities.
- Fourier support can provide a cheaper promised-family transformation.
  Huang et al.'s fixed unamplified circuit accepts supplied copies; its exact
  shortcut uses a suitable support window. Unknown window information and
  pilot samples are charged, and truncation changes the output.
- Exactness belongs to the ideal known-rotation instrument. A finite universal
  gate implementation has a quantified conditional error. The aggregate
  pilot-plus-coherent trial is normalized after averaging its pilot outcomes;
  a tiny-probability transcript cannot be assigned a free error guarantee.
- Collective storage, inverse symmetrization, permutation resources, sparse
  extraction, multiplicity filtering and cleanup are charged. Coherent sorting
  records cannot simply be discarded. No polylogarithmic depth for the whole
  extraction circuit or geometry-optimized architecture is claimed.
- The nonlinear target, elementary postselection, covariance framework,
  qubit filters, collision antecedents and coherent symmetrizer have prior
  sources. Read the attribution before assigning an originality claim.
- Finite checks test normalization, phases, indexing and finite maps. They do
  not prove universal/asymptotic statements or run the complete inherited
  symmetrizer at gate level, and do not constitute external review.
- Arbitrary mixed or drifting sources, unrelated two-source products and
  application-level computational speedups are not established by this result.
